historical_claims.anchor: In the summer of nineteen hundred and one, the Wright brothers went to the dunes of North Carolina with a glider they expected to perform better than their previous machine.
The lift it produced was approximately one third of what their calculations had predicted.
historical_claims.source_locator: Smithsonian 1901 Glider: Back to the Drawing Board / less than forecast lift

historical_claims.anchor: They experimented with a bicycle-based test device and then constructed a small wind tunnel.
The first powered flight lasted twelve seconds.
In April nineteen ninety, the Hubble Space Telescope went into orbit.
During a servicing mission in December nineteen ninety-three, astronauts installed an instrument called COSTAR and a new camera with built-in correction.
historical_claims.source_locator: NASA Servicing Mission 1 and historical review

historical_claims.anchor: A different kind of risk appeared in Cambridge in June nineteen ninety-three, when Andrew Wiles presented what he believed was a proof of Fermat's Last Theorem.
Wiles worked to resolve it, with crucial help from Richard Taylor. A new argument was found in nineteen ninety-four, and the proof appeared in the Annals of Mathematics in nineteen ninety-five.
The first printed installment appeared in eighteen eighty-four. The first edition was not completed until nineteen twenty-eight.
historical_claims.source_locator: Examining the OED first edition chronology

historical_claims.anchor: James Murray, appointed chief editor in eighteen seventy-nine, died in nineteen fifteen, thirteen years before completion.
historical_claims.source_locator: Examining the OED editor chronology and first edition completion
